corpora.note: A tokenizer rather than a corpus. Its digest appears in its own dataset.json group and in the depends_on block of all seven dolma2 corpora, each written by a different sealing pass, and all eight agree. Its seal predates the current shape and records no manifest digest of its own.
Its tokens/manifest.json is byte identical to v6's, 1,793 bytes hashing to 047d001d, so the two entries pin one manifest and hold the same tokens.
v2's token group plus a second group named vendor, holding the five upstream fineweb-edu jsonl.gz files those tokens were built from. Only the payload group is registered.

1,125,064 validation tokens over sixteen payload objects. Not a smaller fineweb-edu-1b: a separate corpus on the same tokenizer, pinning a manifest neither fineweb-edu-1b entry shares. Its .u16le.bin shards make it the one corpus here where OLMo-core's default dtype is the right one.

Text rather than tokens: 25,211 train rows and 300 val over twelve .jsonl objects at profile text-corpus/v1, the Plan A pilot equal-byte multilingual sample. It is what the two gigatoken tokenizers were fitted on.
Equal tokens per language, subsampled from the UniMax 20B arms.
Equal tokens per language, subsampled from the UniMax 20B arms.
Plan B UniMax equal-byte token corpus. 100k-vocab gigatoken BPE.
Plan B UniMax equal-byte token corpus. 100k-vocab gigatoken SuperBPE.
11,862,016 validation tokens over twelve payload objects, packed at sequence length 16,384. v3's own version block declares supersedes of v2, written by the sealing pass on 2026-08-05.

10,059,776 validation tokens over the same twelve payload objects as v2 and 117,833,728 fewer bytes. A revision rather than a re-shard: same tokenizer, same packing, fewer documents. ATP/TPTP traces carry most of the token mass, so a single loss over the whole corpus is mostly measuring two of its six sources.
The frontload-cl early-behaviour-primer pretraining corpus.
Pre-tokenization conversation JSONL, so it declares no tokenizer and has no token count. Registered so admission can resolve it and lineage can name it.
A tokenizer rather than a corpus. Fitted on fineweb2-equal-bytes, 100k vocabulary, and pinned by digest by the Plan B UniMax and Phase-0 corpora.
A tokenizer rather than a corpus. Fitted on fineweb2-equal-bytes, 100k vocabulary, and pinned by digest by the Plan B UniMax and Phase-0 corpora.
226,553 validation tokens over three payload objects.

Pre-tokenization conversation text: 203,324 train rows and 2,078 val over two objects, so there is no token count. `mixed` is a declared answer and is still not a licence: it says the corpus was assembled from sources under more than one without naming them, so anybody redistributing a model trained on it has a question the registry cannot answer.

A verbatim vendor mirror over four .jsonl files with no partitions, so there is no train split to read. Its own limitations block records that any train-ready representation must be a separately validated derived artifact.

Pre-tokenization conversation text: 25,329 train rows and 2,401 val over two objects, so there is no token count. Its own limitations block records that val holds no pedagogy rows and is only the unused no_robots remainder, so a validation loss on it measures ordinary assistant replies rather than teaching.

5,994,057 validation tokens. Two groups and only the payload one is registered: the vendor companion carrying the raw source pull is not, so a reader pinning this entry is pinning the tokens and not the pull.
41 train shards over seven source categories. The dtype was read off a finished run's own checkpoint config on 2026-08-01 rather than off the manifest.

The largest corpus this registry has ever named. 975,077,376 validation tokens over 10,049 payload objects, eight source categories at exact 25,001,984-token shards, held-out documents carved before tokenization. Its licence field says the basis is unknown and its own notes say more: stackexchange and finewiki are CC-BY-SA-4.0, finewiki additionally GFDL, together 17,845,944,320 tokens and 7.13 per cent of train.
A tokenizer rather than a corpus. Its dataset.json names HuggingFaceTB/SmolLM2-135M as its source, which is the fact OLMo-core needs to build it, and both fineweb-edu-1b entries pin its digest.

measured_from: the figures config/datasets.yaml and guides/the-platform.md already carry, read off the sealed dataset.json by whoever registered each corpus. Not a bucket read; tools/build_corpora_snapshot.py replaces this wholesale with one
